generation_rule: A question is eligible only if its core human pain can be stated without IVDIVO lore terms.

questions.question: Who counts as a subject rather than property, infrastructure, evidence or threat?
questions.human_pain: I am being treated as a thing instead of someone whose choice matters.

questions.question: Who has standing to object when the law has no category for them?
questions.human_pain: Something is being done to me, but the system says I am not the kind of person who can object.

questions.question: When does expertise create responsibility without creating command authority?
questions.human_pain: I know something important, but that does not mean everyone must obey me.

questions.question: What makes authority legitimate when several institutions are competent and disagree?
questions.human_pain: The adults in charge all have reasons, but their orders conflict and I must choose whom to trust.

questions.question: Can a protective classification become the mechanism that harms the protected?
questions.human_pain: The rule meant to keep me safe is the thing taking my life away from me.

questions.question: When must an institution revise a category rather than force reality into it?
questions.human_pain: Everyone can see the rule no longer fits, but changing it would admit the system was wrong.

questions.question: How much uncertainty is enough to justify emergency action?
questions.human_pain: If I act too soon I may hurt people; if I wait for certainty it may be too late.

questions.question: Who pays when a lawful decision was reasonable and still caused harm?
questions.human_pain: Nobody was evil, but someone was hurt and responsibility cannot disappear into procedure.

questions.question: Can protection justify overriding a competent person's refusal?
questions.human_pain: The people who love me are trying to save me from a choice that is mine.

questions.question: What counts as consent when minds, bodies or communication methods differ radically?
questions.human_pain: I said yes, but nobody agrees on whether I understood the same thing they did.

questions.question: Can consent remain valid when a person changes during a long process?
questions.human_pain: I agreed as one version of myself and now I am no longer sure that promise belongs to me.

questions.question: Does a parent retain decision power when technology extends childhood, dependency or lifespan?
questions.human_pain: My family still treats me as a child because the old boundary of adulthood no longer works.

questions.question: Can a collective make a choice without every member choosing identically?
questions.human_pain: We belong together, but we do not all want the same future.

questions.question: What information must be disclosed before consent is meaningful?
questions.human_pain: I chose freely, but only because someone hid the part that would have changed my answer.

questions.question: Can the right to withdraw survive when withdrawal endangers others?
questions.human_pain: I want out, but leaving now may hurt people who relied on me.

questions.question: How should systems treat a choice that seems self-destructive but competent?
questions.human_pain: Everyone thinks my decision proves I am unwell because they cannot imagine choosing what I chose.

questions.question: What makes someone the same person after radical physical change?
questions.human_pain: I know I am still me, but the people closest to me no longer recognize the person they loved.

questions.question: Is a perfect copy a continuation, a sibling, evidence, property or a new person?
questions.human_pain: There is another version of me who remembers my life and wants the future I planned.

questions.question: Can continuity survive partial memory loss?
questions.human_pain: I lost pieces of our history; does that mean our relationship has become something else?

questions.question: Who owns memories produced by shared or networked cognition?
questions.human_pain: The most important memory of my life also belongs to people who want it erased or published.

questions.question: How is responsibility assigned across simultaneous embodiments or agents?
questions.human_pain: Another version of me made a choice I would not make, and everyone says I am responsible.

questions.question: When is restoration recovery and when is it replacement?
questions.human_pain: They can bring back everything I used to be, but I do not know whether that would bring me back.

questions.question: Does legal identity follow body, memory, continuity, relationship or declared self?
questions.human_pain: Every system agrees I exist, but each says a different version of me owns my life.

questions.question: What is death when recovery is sometimes possible but never guaranteed?
questions.human_pain: We cannot grieve, wait or move on because nobody can tell us whether the person is gone.

questions.question: Who may read neural, emotional or predictive data?
questions.human_pain: People know things about me I never chose to say.

questions.question: Can safety systems predict danger without turning prediction into punishment?
questions.human_pain: I am being treated as guilty for something a model thinks I might do.

questions.question: Do parents, schools or employers ever own access to another person's inner-state data?
questions.human_pain: The people who control my future demand access to the only place that still feels private.

questions.question: What is betrayal when an AI or partner can infer feelings never spoken aloud?
questions.human_pain: Someone acted on a truth about me that I had not chosen to admit even to myself.

questions.question: Can a person meaningfully refuse surveillance in a life-support-dependent habitat?
questions.human_pain: Privacy is offered as a choice only if I am willing to lose access to ordinary life.

questions.question: Who has the right to forget, delete or seal past versions of the self?
questions.human_pain: My worst moment follows me forever because the system remembers perfectly.

questions.question: Can shared cognition have private rooms?
questions.human_pain: Belonging to the group is real, but I still need a part of myself nobody else can enter.

questions.question: When does cognitive assistance become influence or manipulation?
questions.human_pain: I cannot tell whether I changed my mind or someone made changing it easier than resisting.

questions.question: What is family when people live in different habitats, bodies or timescales?
questions.human_pain: We love each other, but our lives no longer fit in the same place or rhythm.

questions.question: Who is a parent when gestation, genetics, care and design can belong to different people?
questions.human_pain: Several people can truthfully say they made or raised me, and they disagree about who gets to decide.

questions.question: How does longevity change promises of marriage, care and inheritance?
questions.human_pain: A promise that once meant a lifetime may now mean two hundred years of becoming different people.

questions.question: Can love survive radical embodiment without demanding sameness?
questions.human_pain: I love who you are, but I miss the person my body learned to know.

questions.question: What obligations survive when a family member chooses another civilization?
questions.human_pain: Your better future feels like abandonment to the people who cannot follow you.

questions.question: Can care become domination even in an advanced compassionate society?
questions.human_pain: Everyone is helping me so efficiently that there is no room left for my own bad choice.

questions.question: What does fidelity mean across remote or multiple embodiment?
questions.human_pain: We never agreed whether being present in another body counts as being with someone else.

questions.question: How do generations judge parents who built the systems they now reject?
questions.human_pain: I am grateful for the world you built and angry that I have to live inside your compromises.

questions.question: What gives work meaning when automation can outperform most people?
questions.human_pain: I am useful only because the system has not automated me yet.

questions.question: Who gets rare access to bodies, travel, education or frontier work when money is not the only allocator?
questions.human_pain: Nobody is charging me, but I still cannot get the life everyone says is open to all.

questions.question: Can reputation replace money without becoming a social prison?
questions.human_pain: One mistake now determines whether anyone will trust me with anything important.

questions.question: Who owns infrastructure that everyone must use to stay alive?
questions.human_pain: My home depends on a system I cannot leave, change or meaningfully negotiate with.

questions.question: What does property mean for digital, synthetic or distributed beings?
questions.human_pain: The place or machine someone owns is also part of my body or memory.

questions.question: How does a society allocate scarcity after basic material abundance?
questions.human_pain: We have enough to live, but not enough of the things that make one life different from another.

questions.question: Can inherited privilege survive in a society that claims access is earned or universal?
questions.human_pain: Everyone says the system is fair, but the children of insiders always know the doors before I do.

questions.question: Who bears the cost when civilization chooses a safer but slower path?
questions.human_pain: The policy is rational for everyone, but my family is the one that loses the room, job or year.

questions.question: Can a habitat or city be democratic when technical experts control life-critical systems?
questions.human_pain: I get a vote, but the people who understand the machinery can always say my choice is unsafe.

questions.question: What is citizenship when a person belongs to several polities at once?
questions.human_pain: Every place claims part of me and none accepts responsibility for all of me.

questions.question: How should punishment work in a closed habitat where exile may equal death?
questions.human_pain: The community must stay safe, but every ordinary punishment has become extreme.

questions.question: Can rehabilitation become coercive optimization?
questions.human_pain: The system can make me less dangerous by changing the parts of me I still consider mine.

questions.question: Who governs Earth-orbit problems that no single sovereignty can solve?
questions.human_pain: Everyone has legitimate authority over part of the crisis and nobody can act over the whole.

questions.question: When may a more capable civilization intervene in a less capable one?
questions.human_pain: They could stop our suffering, but accepting their help may mean surrendering the right to make our own mistakes.

questions.question: How can institutions confess old crimes without destroying useful present legitimacy?
questions.human_pain: The people protecting us today inherited a lie that hurt people like me yesterday.

questions.question: Can emergency powers end cleanly after the emergency?
questions.human_pain: The rule that saved us is still controlling us after the danger passed.

questions.question: Can an ecology, city or distributed system have standing without being humanlike?
questions.human_pain: Something we depend on is being destroyed because it cannot ask for help in our language.

questions.question: What obligations exist to forms of life whose needs conflict with human settlement?
questions.human_pain: My home and someone else's survival cannot both continue unchanged.

questions.question: When is terraforming creation and when is it erasure?
questions.human_pain: We can make this place livable for us only by ending what it is now.

questions.question: How should first contact proceed when both sides misclassify the other?
questions.human_pain: We hurt each other because each side thought the other's warning was an attack.

questions.question: Can a mature civilization admit that its own frontier is genuinely unknown?
questions.human_pain: The people I trusted because they knew more are afraid too, and now I must decide without an oracle.

questions.question: Who may accept frontier risk on behalf of people who benefit but never consented?
questions.human_pain: Someone else's brave experiment can change the world I am forced to live in.

questions.question: What knowledge should remain deliberately inaccessible?
questions.human_pain: The answer exists, but learning it may change us in ways nobody can reverse.

questions.question: What does progress mean when every solved boundary reveals a larger unknown?
questions.human_pain: We finally reached the future we dreamed of and discovered that it still cannot tell us how to live.
